public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 785

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/785](https://www.erdosproblems.com/785)
- [ChFa10] Fang, Jin-Hui and Chen, Yong-Gao, *On additive complements*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (2010), 1923-1927.
- [ChFa11] Chen, Yong-Gao and Fang, Jin-Hui, *On additive complements. II*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (2011), 881-883.
- [ChFa14] Fang, Jin-Hui and Chen, Yong-Gao, *On additive complements. III*. J. Number Theory
  (2014), 83-91.
- [ChFa15] Chen, Yong-Gao and Fang, Jin-Hui, *On a conjecture of Sárközy and Szemerédi*.
  Acta Arith. (2015), 47-58.
- [Da64] Danzer, L., *Über eine Frage von G. Hanani aus der additiven Zahlentheorie*.
  J. Reine Angew. Math. (1964), 392-394.
- [Er57] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Michigan Math. J. (1957), 291-300.
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Na59] Narkiewicz, Władysław, *Remarks on a conjecture of Hanani in additive number theory*.
  Colloq. Math. (1959/60), 161-165.
- [Ru17] Ruzsa, Imre Z., *Exact additive complements*. Q. J. Math. (2017), 227-235.
- [SaSz94] Sárközy, A. and Szemerédi, E., *On a problem in additive number theory*.
  Acta Math. Hungar. (1994), 237-245.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Pointwise
open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos785

/-- The counting function $A(x)=\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert$. -/
noncomputable def counting (A : Set ℕ) (x : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (A ∩ Set.Icc 1 x).ncard

/-- The largest element of $A$ in $[1,x]$, that is $a^*(x)=\max A\cap [1,x]$
(equal to $0$ when there is no such element). -/
noncomputable def aStar (A : Set ℕ) (x : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup (A ∩ Set.Icc 1 x)

/-- Two sets $A, B\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ are *exact additive complements* if $A+B$ contains all
large integers and $A(x)B(x)\sim x$. -/
def IsExactAdditiveComplement (A B : Set ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsAdditiveComplement A B ∧
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1)

/--
Let $A,B\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be infinite sets of positive integers such that $A+B$ contains all
large integers. Let $A(x)=\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert$ and similarly for $B(x)$. Is it true that if
$A(x)B(x)\sim x$ then
$$A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$$
as $x\to \infty$?

A conjecture of Erdős and Danzer. The answer is yes, proved by Sárközy and Szemerédi [SaSz94],
who actually proved that it is impossible for
$$A(x)B(x)-x=o(A(x)).$$

This was formalized in Lean by van Doorn using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
"https://github.com/Woett/Lean-files/blob/main/ErdosProblem785.lean"]
theorem erdos_785 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → B.Infinite → 0 ∉ A → 0 ∉ B → IsExactAdditiveComplement A B →
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Danzer [Da64] proved that exact additive complements exist (Hanani had earlier conjectured they
do not exist, as reported in [Er57] and [Er61]).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.danzer :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ 0 ∉ B ∧ IsExactAdditiveComplement A B := by
  sorry

/--
Sárközy and Szemerédi [SaSz94] proved that it is impossible for
$$A(x)B(x)-x=o(A(x)).$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.sarkozy_szemeredi (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    ¬ (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Chen and Fang [ChFa15] proved $A(x)B(x)-x\ll \min(A(x),B(x))^c$ cannot hold for any constant
$c>0$. In particular $A(x)B(x)-x\ll A(x)^c$ cannot hold when $A$ is the sparser of the two sets.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) :
    ¬ (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ => (min (counting A x) (counting B x) : ℝ) ^ c) := by
  sorry

/--
Narkiewicz [Na59] proved that, under the given assumptions (and perhaps swapping $A$ and $B$)
we must have $A(2x)/A(x)\to 1$ and $B(2x)/B(x)\to 2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.narkiewicz (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting B (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 2)) ∨
    (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting B (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ))
        atTop (𝓝 2)) := by
  sorry

/--
Ruzsa [Ru17] has constructed, for any function $w(x)\to \infty$, such a pair of sets with
$$A(x)B(x)-x<w(x)$$
for infinitely many $x$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_upper_bound (w : ℕ → ℝ) (hw : Tendsto w atTop atTop) :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ 0 ∉ B ∧ IsExactAdditiveComplement A B ∧
      ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) < w x := by
  sorry

/--
Ruzsa [Ru17] proves that, if $a^*(x)=\max A \cap [1,x]$ and $A$ and $B$ satisfy the conditions
in the problem then (after possibly changing the roles of $A$ and $B$)
$$A(x)B(x)-x > (1-o(1))\frac{a^*(x)}{A(x)}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_lower_bound (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
        (1 - ε) * (aStar A x : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)
          < (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) ∨
    (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
        (1 - ε) * (aStar B x : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)
          < (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Chen and Fang [ChFa10] proved the stronger statement that $A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$ if $A$ and $B$
are infinite sets such that $A+B$ contains all large integers and
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}<\frac{5}{4}.$$
They later [ChFa14] improved $5/4$ to $3-\sqrt{3}\approx 1.268$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_limsup (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsAdditiveComplement A B)
    (hlim : limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
      < ((3 - Real.sqrt 3 : ℝ) : EReal)) :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Chen conjectures that this should be true with $3/2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → B.Infinite → 0 ∉ A → 0 ∉ B → IsAdditiveComplement A B →
      limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
          < ((3 / 2 : ℝ) : EReal) →
        Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
This is sharp, as Chen and Fang [ChFa11] also proved that there exist such $A$ and $B$ with
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}=\frac{3}{2}$$
for which $A(x)B(x)-x=1$ for infinitely many $x$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_sharp :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ 0 ∉ B ∧ IsAdditiveComplement A B ∧
      limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
          = ((3 / 2 : ℝ) : EReal) ∧
      ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) = 1 := by
  sorry

end Erdos785

findings.description:
The conclusion `¬ (fun x => A(x)B(x) - x) =o[atTop] (fun x => A(x))` unfolds to: for some ε > 0, |A(x)B(x) − x| > ε·A(x) for infinitely many x. This is trivially true for EVERY pair of infinite additive complements of positive integers, exact or not.

Proof: if every n ≥ N lies in A+B, then A(y)B(y) ≥ y+1−N for all y. At each b ∈ B, B(b) = B(b−1)+1, so A(b)B(b) − b ≥ A(b) − N, and A(b) → ∞.

I proved the declaration's exact type in a scratch file (/workspace/review/ss_trivial.lean, ~100 elementary lines; `#print axioms`: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The proof uses only `h.1 : IsAdditiveComplement A B`, never the exactness condition A(x)B(x)/x → 1.

So the statement also holds for non-exact pairs, e.g. the Chen–Fang [ChFa11] sets shifted to positive integers, where A(x)B(x) − x = 1 for infinitely many x (checked numerically at x = 4^k − 1). It does not imply the main theorem A(x)B(x) − x → ∞.

The source presents SS's result as a strengthening of that answer ("who actually proved"). The intended content is that o(A(x)) fails even along subsequences for the sparse set A. In other words, A(x)B(x) − x ≫ A(x) = min(A(x),B(x)) for all large x. This is the eventual form that Chen–Fang [ChFa15, Thm 0.2] and Ruzsa improve.
findings.source_evidence:
erdosproblems.com/785 (Wayback snapshot 2026-07-09): "The answer is yes, proved by Sárközy and Szemerédi [SaSz94], who actually proved that it is impossible for A(x)B(x)−x=o(A(x)). This was improved by Chen and Fang [ChFa15]..."

Ruzsa, Exact additive complements, arXiv:1510.00812 §1: "For the sequel we will assume that (smallbig) holds, that is, A is small and B is large. ... They remark that their proof shows that A(x)B(x)−x = o(A(x)) cannot hold, and they conjecture that A(x)B(x)−x = O(A(x)) may be possible."

Chen–Fang, Acta Arith. 169 (2015) 47–58: Conjecture 0.1 (SS) "A(x)B(x) − x = O(min{A(x),B(x)})"; Theorem 0.2 "A(x)B(x) − x ≥ (min{A(x),B(x)})^M for all sufficiently large integers x".
findings.suggested_fix:
State the eventual lower bound for the sparse set:
`∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, c * (min (counting A x) (counting B x) : ℝ) ≤ (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)`

Using `min` picks out the sparse set. With plain `counting A x` under the symmetric ∀ A B, the eventual bound would be false for the dense set, by Ruzsa's example with A(x)B(x) − x < ω(x) infinitely often. The fix elaborates (/workspace/review/fixes.lean) and follows from [ChFa15, Thm 0.2].

findings.description:
The Lean states, for each c > 0, `¬ (fun x => A(x)B(x) − x) =O[atTop] (fun x => min(A(x),B(x))^c)`. That is: for every C, |A(x)B(x) − x| > C·min^c for infinitely many x (a limsup statement).

[ChFa15] proves an eventual lower bound: for every M > 1, A(x)B(x) − x ≥ min{A(x),B(x)}^M for ALL sufficiently large x. That theorem implies A(x)B(x) − x → ∞ and disproves the SS conjecture.

The Lean statement is far weaker. It follows from Narkiewicz's growth bounds alone (for the sparse A, A(x) < x^δ and B(x) > x^{1−δ} eventually; Ruzsa's Thm 1.1 (1.4)) plus the elementary jump A(a)B(a) − a ≥ B(a) − N at each a ∈ A. I proved this implication in Lean (/workspace/review/cf_weak.lean, `cf_from_growth`, sorry-free), with no input from Chen–Fang.

As a property of a pair it constrains only the limsup of |A(x)B(x) − x|/min^c. It says nothing about most x, so unlike the cited theorem it does not yield the main result or improve on SS.
findings.source_evidence:
Chen–Fang, "On a conjecture of Sárközy and Szemerédi", Acta Arith. 169 (2015), 47–48: "In this paper, we disprove this conjecture. In fact, the following stronger result is proved. Theorem 0.2. For infinite additive complements A, B, if (0.1) holds, then, for any given M > 1, we have A(x)B(x) − x ≥ (min{A(x),B(x)})^M for all sufficiently large integers x." The same appears as Theorem 7 in Chen's Graz 2016 slides.

erdosproblems.com/785: "This was improved by Chen and Fang [ChFa15], who proved A(x)B(x)−x≪A(x)^c cannot hold for any constant c>0."
findings.suggested_fix:
Replace the conclusion by [ChFa15, Theorem 0.2]:
`(M : ℝ) (hM : 1 < M) : ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (min (counting A x) (counting B x) : ℝ) ^ M ≤ (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)`

Equivalently: ∀ c > 0, ∀ C, ∀ᶠ x, C * min(A(x),B(x))^c < A(x)B(x) − x. This elaborates (/workspace/review/fixes.lean).

findings.description:
The conclusion is a disjunction: the bound (1−ε)a*(x)/A(x) < A(x)B(x) − x holds eventually with A, OR the analogous bound holds with B. Ruzsa's Theorem 1.2 fixes the roles: A is the sparse set of Narkiewicz's dichotomy, with A(2x)/A(x) → 1.

The disjunct with the DENSE set in that role is weak. For the dense set, b*(x)/B(x) ≤ x/B(x) ≤ A(x) + O(1/B(x)), so that disjunct only asks A(x)B(x) − x to exceed about (1−ε)·(count of the sparse set). This already follows from [ChFa15, Thm 0.2] with M = 2 plus "A is eventually the sparser set" (Narkiewicz). I proved this in Lean (/workspace/review/ruzsa_weak.lean, `ruzsa_disj_from_cf`, sorry-free).

So the declaration is a consequence of [ChFa15] + [Na59] and does not state Ruzsa's improvement, whose right-hand side a*(x)/A(x) grows faster than any power of A(x). The source's own remark right after the bound assumes A is the sparse set.
findings.source_evidence:
Ruzsa, arXiv:1510.00812, Theorem 1.2: "Suppose they satisfy (hyp) and the notation corresponds to (smallbig) [A(2x)/A(x)→1, B(2x)/B(x)→2]. If r(x) = o(a*(x)), then A(x)B(x) − x > (1 − o(1)) a*(x)/A(x)."

erdosproblems.com/785: "...(after possibly changing the roles of A and B) A(x)B(x)−x > (1−o(1)) a*(x)/A(x). (Note that Narkiewicz' result implies A(x) < a*(x)^{o(1)}, so the right-hand side grows faster than any power of A(x).)"

The linked formal proof (van Doorn, ErdosProblem785.lean, `theorem_estimate`) carries the hypothesis `h_smallbig_A`.
findings.suggested_fix:
Pin the roles to the sparse set. Add
`(hsmall : Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1))`
and conclude only
`∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (1 - ε) * (aStar A x : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ) < (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)`
(elaborates in /workspace/review/fixes.lean).

Alternatively, state the bound for whichever set has the eventually smaller counting function.

reformulations.difference: Chen states the conjecture for 'infinite additive complements': infinite sequences of NON-NEGATIVE integers (repetitions allowed), counted by T(x) = |T ∩ [0,x]|. The Lean uses sets of POSITIVE integers (`0 ∉ A`, `0 ∉ B`) counted on [1,x].
[ChFa10]/[ChFa14] are stated for sequences of non-negative integers counted on [0,x]. The Lean uses sets of positive integers (`0 ∉ A`, `0 ∉ B`) counted on [1,x].
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The shift T ↦ T+1 (and removal of multiplicities) preserves the additive-complement property, infinitude, limsup A(x)B(x)/x, and A(x)B(x) − x → ∞, since (T+1)(x) = T(x−1) and the quantity shifts by the constant −1. So the Lean statement with 3 − √3 is equivalent to Fang–Chen's Theorem ([ChFa14]; Chen's slides, Theorem 5).

could_not_verify: Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.sarkozy_szemeredi — the original [SaSz94] (Acta Math. Hungar. 64 (1994), paywalled) was not accessible. The precise form of SS's remark comes from Ruzsa (arXiv:1510.00812) and Chen–Fang (Acta Arith. 2015). The finding (the Lean statement is provable without exactness) does not depend on it; only the exact shape of the suggested fix (constant c, use of min) does.
review.notes:
**Scratch files** (all in /workspace/review; the checkout is untouched):
- `ss_trivial.lean` proves the exact type of `erdos_785.variants.sarkozy_szemeredi` from `IsAdditiveComplement` alone (axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound).
- `cf_weak.lean` derives the `chen_fang` statement from Narkiewicz-type growth bounds plus the jump argument.
- `ruzsa_weak.lean` derives the dense-set disjunct of `ruzsa_lower_bound` from Chen–Fang Theorem 0.2 (M = 2) plus eventual sparsity of A.
- `fixes.lean` shows the suggested replacements elaborate.
- `cf_sharp_eval.lean` numerically checks the shifted Chen–Fang (a = 2) construction.

**Why `sarkozy_szemeredi` and `chen_fang` need the eventual form.** Taken literally ("A(x)B(x)−x = o(A(x)) is impossible", "≪ A(x)^c cannot hold"), the website's phrases are near-trivial because of the jump at set elements. The literature's content is the eventual form: SS's remark, [ChFa15] Theorem 0.2 "for all sufficiently large x", and Ruzsa's Theorem 1.2.

**Conventions.** Chen–Fang use non-negative sequences with T(x) = |T∩[0,x]|. Ruzsa, the website and van Doorn use positive integers with [1,x]. The Lean's `0 ∉ A, 0 ∉ B` plus [1,x] counting is equivalent for every asymptotic statement here, via the shift.

**`chen_fang_sharp`.** The one convention-sensitive value is the "= 1". The literal shift of [ChFa11]'s "A(x)B(x) − x = 1 i.o." gives "= 0 at x = 4^k". The Lean's "= 1" still holds for the shifted sets at x = 4^k − 1, and the sumset covers [2, ∞) with sup ratio → 3/2 (verified numerically). The declaration is true and matches the website's wording, just marginally weaker than [ChFa11]; not reported.

**Status.**
- `erdos_785`: research solved with a `formal_proof`, consistent with the site's 'PROVED (LEAN)'. The linked file proves the same positive-integer statement over real x, which is equivalent.
- `chen_conjecture` (3/2) is still open. Yang–Zhao (arXiv:2609.13900, Sept 2026) improve 3 − √3 to 4/3, so `chen_fang_limsup` could be strengthened, but it stays true as stated.

**Other declarations.** `danzer`, `narkiewicz` and `chen_fang_limsup` were checked against the statements quoted in Ruzsa (Thm 1.1), Chen–Fang 2011/2015 and Chen's slides; the originals (Da64, Na59, ChFa10, ChFa14) were not accessed. `ruzsa_upper_bound` matches Ruzsa's Theorem 1.3; it drops the c·a*(x) part, as the website does.

demonstrated.claim: The declaration's exact type (via `type_of%`) is proved with its hypotheses `0 ∉ A`, `0 ∉ B` and `IsExactAdditiveComplement A B` discarded: for any two infinite A, B ⊆ ℕ, A(x)B(x) − x jumps by at least A(b) − 1 at each b ∈ B, so it is never o(A(x)); a statement true for every pair of infinite sets cannot express the Sárközy–Szemerédi result.

not_demonstrated.reason: The declaration is true, just much weaker than [ChFa15, Theorem 0.2], so there is nothing false to refute. Proving it as stated for c ≥ 1 needs Narkiewicz's dichotomy (A(x) < x^δ, B(x) > x^{1−δ} for the sparse set), which is real mathematics. I only have a derivation from those growth bounds taken as a hypothesis (/workspace/review/cf_weak.lean, about 80 lines), not a short proof of the declaration.

The declaration is true, just weaker than Ruzsa's Theorem 1.2, since its disjunct for the dense set already follows from [ChFa15, Thm 0.2] plus Narkiewicz. Proving it as stated needs one of those deep theorems. My Lean evidence (/workspace/review/ruzsa_weak.lean) derives the dense-set disjunct from those results taken as hypotheses; that is not a short proof of the declaration.

`/workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean` (69 lines) compiles cleanly: `lake env lean --json` reports no errors, no warnings and no `sorry`. `#print axioms` on a throwaway copy lists only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

The file proves `erdos_785.variants.sarkozy_szemeredi` exactly as stated: `example : type_of% @Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.sarkozy_szemeredi := fun A B hA hB _ _ _ => not_isLittleO A B hA hB`. The helper `not_isLittleO` shows that for any two infinite sets A, B ⊆ ℕ, `A(x)B(x) − x` is not o(A(x)). The argument is elementary: at each b ∈ B the counting function B jumps by 1, so A(x)B(x) − x rises by at least A(b) − 1. It therefore cannot stay within ±A(x)/8 at both b − 1 and b once A(b) ≥ 2. Neither the positivity hypotheses nor exactness is used, so the declaration cannot state the Sárközy–Szemerédi strengthening of A(x)B(x) − x → ∞.

The `chen_fang` and `ruzsa_lower_bound` findings are about the formal statements being much weaker than the cited theorems (Chen–Fang 2015, Ruzsa 2017). Both are true as stated, and proving them needs Narkiewicz's dichotomy or Chen–Fang's theorem, so they get no trivial demonstration. Nothing under /opt/formal-conjectures was modified.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«785»

/-!
Trivial proof for `Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.sarkozy_szemeredi`.
-/

open Filter Erdos785

namespace TrivialProof

lemma counting_mono (A : Set ℕ) {x y : ℕ} (h : x ≤ y) : counting A x ≤ counting A y :=
  Set.ncard_le_ncard (fun _ hn => ⟨hn.1, hn.2.1, hn.2.2.trans h⟩)
    ((Set.finite_Icc 1 y).inter_of_right A)

/-- `B(b) ≥ B(b - 1) + 1` when `1 ≤ b ∈ B`. -/
lemma counting_jump (B : Set ℕ) {b : ℕ} (hb : b ∈ B) (hb1 : 1 ≤ b) :
    counting B (b - 1) + 1 ≤ counting B b := by
  have hnot : b ∉ B ∩ Set.Icc 1 (b - 1) := fun h => by have := h.2.2; omega
  unfold counting
  rw [← Set.ncard_insert_of_notMem hnot ((Set.finite_Icc 1 (b - 1)).inter_of_right B)]
  refine Set.ncard_le_ncard ?_ ((Set.finite_Icc 1 b).inter_of_right B)
  rintro n (rfl | ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩)
  · exact ⟨hb, hb1, le_rfl⟩
  · exact ⟨h1, h2, by omega⟩

/-- The conclusion of `sarkozy_szemeredi` holds for ANY two infinite sets `A, B ⊆ ℕ`:
`A(x)B(x) - x` jumps by at least `A(b) - 1` at every `b ∈ B`, so it cannot stay within
`± A(x)/8`. -/
theorem not_isLittleO (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite) :
    ¬ (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x : ℝ)) := by
  intro ho
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := eventually_atTop.mp (ho.bound (show (0 : ℝ) < 1 / 8 by norm_num))
  obtain ⟨a₁, ha₁, h₁⟩ := hA.exists_gt 0
  obtain ⟨a₂, ha₂, h₂⟩ := hA.exists_gt a₁
  obtain ⟨b, hb, hbN⟩ := hB.exists_gt (N + a₂)
  have hA2 : 2 ≤ counting A b := by
    rw [← Set.ncard_pair (show a₁ ≠ a₂ by omega)]
    refine Set.ncard_le_ncard ?_ ((Set.finite_Icc 1 b).inter_of_right A)
    rintro n (rfl | rfl)
    · exact ⟨ha₁, by omega, by omega⟩
    · exact ⟨ha₂, by omega, by omega⟩
  have hjump : (counting B (b - 1) : ℝ) + 1 ≤ counting B b := by
    exact_mod_cast counting_jump B hb (by omega)
  have hmono : (counting A (b - 1) : ℝ) ≤ counting A b := by
    exact_mod_cast counting_mono A (show b - 1 ≤ b by omega)
  have hA2' : (2 : ℝ) ≤ counting A b := by exact_mod_cast hA2
  have hcast : ((b - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) = (b : ℝ) - 1 := by
    rw [Nat.cast_sub (show 1 ≤ b by omega), Nat.cast_one]
  have h1 := hN b (by omega)
  have h2 := hN (b - 1) (by omega)
  rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, Real.norm_eq_abs,
    abs_of_nonneg (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) ≤ counting A b)] at h1
  rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, Real.norm_eq_abs,
    abs_of_nonneg (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) ≤ counting A (b - 1)), hcast] at h2
  have hB0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ counting B (b - 1) := by positivity
  have p1 : (counting A b : ℝ) * (counting B (b - 1) + 1) ≤ counting A b * counting B b :=
    mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hjump (by positivity)
  have p2 : (counting A (b - 1) : ℝ) * counting B (b - 1) ≤ counting A b * counting B (b - 1) :=
    mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hmono hB0
  linarith [(abs_le.mp h1).2, (abs_le.mp h2).1]

/-- `Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.sarkozy_szemeredi`: provable (trivially true) — its hypotheses
`0 ∉ A`, `0 ∉ B` and `IsExactAdditiveComplement A B` are never used, so it cannot express the
Sárközy–Szemerédi strengthening of `A(x)B(x) - x → ∞`. -/
example : type_of% @Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.sarkozy_szemeredi :=
  fun A B hA hB _ _ _ => not_isLittleO A B hA hB

end TrivialProof

submission.summary:
I fixed the three reported declarations in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/785.lean`. The file compiles: `lake env lean --json` exits 0 with 10 messages, all `declaration uses 'sorry'`, and no errors. It is also clean with the lakefile's repository linters passed as `-D` flags, and no line is longer than 100 characters. Nothing else in the checkout was touched. (`lakefile.toml` and `run/` already showed as modified at 12:21, before this work started.)

1. **`erdos_785.variants.sarkozy_szemeredi`.** The old conclusion `¬ (A(x)B(x) − x) =o[atTop] A(x)` held for any two infinite sets, so it said nothing. It now states the eventual lower bound: `∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ x in atTop, c * min(A(x), B(x)) ≤ A(x)B(x) − x`. Using `min` picks out the sparse set; with plain A(x), the symmetric ∀ A B would make the bound false for the dense set. The docstring now says "where A is the sparser set, even along a subsequence". The statement implies the main theorem and follows from Chen–Fang 2015, Theorem 0.2.

2. **`erdos_785.variants.chen_fang`.** `(c) (hc : 0 < c)` with `¬ … =O[atTop] min(A,B)^c` is replaced by the paper's Theorem 0.2: `(M : ℝ) (hM : 1 < M) : ∀ᶠ x in atTop, min(A(x), B(x))^M ≤ A(x)B(x) − x`. The docstring keeps the website's "≪ min^c cannot hold" sentence and adds the exact theorem.

3. **`erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_lower_bound`.** The "A or B" disjunction is replaced by Ruzsa's Theorem 1.2 with the roles fixed. The new hypothesis `hsmall` says A is the sparse set: `Tendsto (fun x => A(2x)/A(x)) atTop (𝓝 1)`, the same expression as in the file's `narkiewicz` variant. The conclusion is now the single bound for A. The docstring adds one sentence saying which set A is.

Categories, AMS tags, references and every other declaration are unchanged. I checked that the new types elaborate as intended by compiling a throwaway copy of the edited file with `#check` lines. The earlier `trivial_proof.lean` example no longer applies to the corrected `sarkozy_szemeredi`, as intended.

module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 785

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/785](https://www.erdosproblems.com/785)
- [ChFa10] Fang, Jin-Hui and Chen, Yong-Gao, *On additive complements*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (2010), 1923-1927.
- [ChFa11] Chen, Yong-Gao and Fang, Jin-Hui, *On additive complements. II*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (2011), 881-883.
- [ChFa14] Fang, Jin-Hui and Chen, Yong-Gao, *On additive complements. III*. J. Number Theory
  (2014), 83-91.
- [ChFa15] Chen, Yong-Gao and Fang, Jin-Hui, *On a conjecture of Sárközy and Szemerédi*.
  Acta Arith. (2015), 47-58.
- [Da64] Danzer, L., *Über eine Frage von G. Hanani aus der additiven Zahlentheorie*.
  J. Reine Angew. Math. (1964), 392-394.
- [Er57] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Michigan Math. J. (1957), 291-300.
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Na59] Narkiewicz, Władysław, *Remarks on a conjecture of Hanani in additive number theory*.
  Colloq. Math. (1959/60), 161-165.
- [Ru17] Ruzsa, Imre Z., *Exact additive complements*. Q. J. Math. (2017), 227-235.
- [SaSz94] Sárközy, A. and Szemerédi, E., *On a problem in additive number theory*.
  Acta Math. Hungar. (1994), 237-245.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Pointwise
open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos785

/-- The counting function $A(x)=\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert$. -/
noncomputable def counting (A : Set ℕ) (x : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (A ∩ Set.Icc 1 x).ncard

/-- The largest element of $A$ in $[1,x]$, that is $a^*(x)=\max A\cap [1,x]$
(equal to $0$ when there is no such element). -/
noncomputable def aStar (A : Set ℕ) (x : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup (A ∩ Set.Icc 1 x)

/-- Two sets $A, B\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ are *exact additive complements* if $A+B$ contains all
large integers and $A(x)B(x)\sim x$. -/
def IsExactAdditiveComplement (A B : Set ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsAdditiveComplement A B ∧
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1)

/--
Let $A,B\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be infinite sets of positive integers such that $A+B$ contains all
large integers. Let $A(x)=\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert$ and similarly for $B(x)$. Is it true that if
$A(x)B(x)\sim x$ then
$$A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$$
as $x\to \infty$?

A conjecture of Erdős and Danzer. The answer is yes, proved by Sárközy and Szemerédi [SaSz94],
who actually proved that it is impossible for
$$A(x)B(x)-x=o(A(x)).$$

This was formalized in Lean by van Doorn using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
"https://github.com/Woett/Lean-files/blob/main/ErdosProblem785.lean"]
theorem erdos_785 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → B.Infinite → 0 ∉ A → 0 ∉ B → IsExactAdditiveComplement A B →
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Danzer [Da64] proved that exact additive complements exist (Hanani had earlier conjectured they
do not exist, as reported in [Er57] and [Er61]).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.danzer :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ 0 ∉ B ∧ IsExactAdditiveComplement A B := by
  sorry

/--
Sárközy and Szemerédi [SaSz94] proved that it is impossible for
$$A(x)B(x)-x=o(A(x)),$$
where $A$ is the sparser of the two sets, even along a subsequence. That is, there is $c>0$ with
$A(x)B(x)-x\geq c\min(A(x),B(x))$ for all large $x$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.sarkozy_szemeredi (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (min (counting A x) (counting B x) : ℝ) ≤
        (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Chen and Fang [ChFa15] proved $A(x)B(x)-x\ll \min(A(x),B(x))^c$ cannot hold for any constant
$c>0$. In fact, for every $M>1$ we have $A(x)B(x)-x\geq \min(A(x),B(x))^M$ for all large $x$.
In particular $A(x)B(x)-x\ll A(x)^c$ cannot hold when $A$ is the sparser of the two sets.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 < M) :
    ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
      (min (counting A x) (counting B x) : ℝ) ^ M ≤
        (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Narkiewicz [Na59] proved that, under the given assumptions (and perhaps swapping $A$ and $B$)
we must have $A(2x)/A(x)\to 1$ and $B(2x)/B(x)\to 2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.narkiewicz (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting B (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 2)) ∨
    (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting B (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ))
        atTop (𝓝 2)) := by
  sorry

/--
Ruzsa [Ru17] has constructed, for any function $w(x)\to \infty$, such a pair of sets with
$$A(x)B(x)-x<w(x)$$
for infinitely many $x$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_upper_bound (w : ℕ → ℝ) (hw : Tendsto w atTop atTop) :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ 0 ∉ B ∧ IsExactAdditiveComplement A B ∧
      ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) < w x := by
  sorry

/--
Ruzsa [Ru17] proves that, if $a^*(x)=\max A \cap [1,x]$ and $A$ and $B$ satisfy the conditions
in the problem then (after possibly changing the roles of $A$ and $B$)
$$A(x)B(x)-x > (1-o(1))\frac{a^*(x)}{A(x)}.$$
Here $A$ is the sparser set in Narkiewicz's dichotomy, that is $A(2x)/A(x)\to 1$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_lower_bound (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B)
    (hsmall : Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1)) :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
      (1 - ε) * (aStar A x : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)
        < (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Chen and Fang [ChFa10] proved the stronger statement that $A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$ if $A$ and $B$
are infinite sets such that $A+B$ contains all large integers and
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}<\frac{5}{4}.$$
They later [ChFa14] improved $5/4$ to $3-\sqrt{3}\approx 1.268$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_limsup (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsAdditiveComplement A B)
    (hlim : limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
      < ((3 - Real.sqrt 3 : ℝ) : EReal)) :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Chen conjectures that this should be true with $3/2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → B.Infinite → 0 ∉ A → 0 ∉ B → IsAdditiveComplement A B →
      limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
          < ((3 / 2 : ℝ) : EReal) →
        Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
This is sharp, as Chen and Fang [ChFa11] also proved that there exist such $A$ and $B$ with
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}=\frac{3}{2}$$
for which $A(x)B(x)-x=1$ for infinitely many $x$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_sharp :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ 0 ∉ B ∧ IsAdditiveComplement A B ∧
      limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
          = ((3 / 2 : ℝ) : EReal) ∧
      ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) = 1 := by
  sorry

end Erdos785
